title: Capstone: Time-series & ML
text: Built a forecasting pipeline to predict future metrics for a stock price changes.

title: Capstone: Time-series & ML
text: Built a forecasting pipeline to predict future metrics for a stock price changes.

title: Capstone: Time-series & ML
text:
Data
Combined multiple data sources from macroeconomic, microeconomic, historical stock price, and sentiment data. Webscraping and APIs were used to gather these

title: Capstone: Time-series & ML
text:
Approach

Cleaned and merged time-series
Explored patterns and seasonality
Trained RandomForest, TFT, and LSTM models

title: Capstone: Time-series & ML
text:
Results
The RandomForest model was the most accurate but not accurate enough when it comes to yearly predictions

title: Capstone: Time-series & ML
text:
Top Correlations by Horizon



Top 10 features correlated with returns at 1‑day/1‑week/1‑month/1‑year. Short‑term is sentiment‑heavy (news/Reddit, PPI), while longer horizons shift to macro fundamentals (housing starts, retail sales, PCE, GDP).

title: Capstone: Time-series & ML
section: 30‑Day MA: Price vs Positive News Sentiment
text:
30‑Day MA: Price vs Positive News Sentiment



MSFT closing price plotted against positive‑news sentiment . Broad co‑movement shows optimism tends to align with price uptrends.

title: Capstone: Time-series & ML
section: High Positive Sentiment Events on Price
text:
High Positive Sentiment Events on Price



Red markers flag dates with unusually high positive sentiment overlaid on price.

title: Capstone: Time-series & ML
text:
1‑Day Ahead: Actual vs Predicted (Random Forest)



RF predictions (orange) versus actual 1‑day returns. Captures direction reasonably but smooths away extreme spikes.

title: Capstone: Time-series & ML
text:
1‑Day Ahead: Actual vs Predicted (LightGBM)



LGBM 1‑day forecasts. Smoother than actuals; tracks trend changes with modest lag and underestimates large moves.

title: Capstone: Time-series & ML
text:
1‑Day Ahead: Actual vs Predicted (XGBoost)



XGB 1‑day forecasts. Similar bias toward conservative magnitudes, with stable tracking of mean‑reverting behavior.

title: Capstone: Time-series & ML
text:
1‑Week Ahead: Actual vs Predicted (Random Forest)



RF 1‑week horizon. Directional fit remains, but volatility amplification at this horizon widens miss on extremes.

title: Capstone: Time-series & ML
text:
1‑Week Ahead: Actual vs Predicted (LightGBM)



LGBM 1‑week forecasts. Predictions stay close to zero and change slowly, good at trend, weak on amplitude.

title: Capstone: Time-series & ML
text:
1‑Week Ahead: Actual vs Predicted (XGBoost)



XGB 1‑week horizon. Best smoothness among the three but still underestimates sharp drops/spikes typical of weekly returns.

title: Capstone: Time-series & ML
text:

title: Diabetes: EDA & Modeling
text: Investigated factors associated with diabetes progression to inform preventative care.

title: Diabetes: EDA & Modeling
text: Investigated factors associated with diabetes progression to inform preventative care.

title: Diabetes: EDA & Modeling
text:
Data
Used the publicly available dataset of patient measurements from the UCI repository.

title: Diabetes: EDA & Modeling
text:
Approach

Cleaned outliers and imputed missing values
Visualized relationships among clinical variables
Trained logistic regression and random forest classifiers

title: Diabetes: EDA & Modeling
text:
Results
The tuned random forest reached 82% accuracy and highlighted BMI and glucose as key features.

title: Diabetes: EDA & Modeling
text:
Pair Plot of Features



Pairwise relationships between key health features (glucose, BMI, age, etc.) with diabetes outcome. Highlights clusters and potential separability between classes.

title: Diabetes: EDA & Modeling
text:
Feature Distributions by Outcome



Distribution of each feature split by diabetes diagnosis. Shows clear separation for glucose and BMI between positive and negative cases.

title: Diabetes: EDA & Modeling
text:
Correlation Heatmap



Correlation matrix of all features with outcome. Glucose and BMI show the strongest relationships with diabetes.

title: Diabetes: EDA & Modeling
section: Outcome by BMI, Age, and Pregnancy Risk
text:
Outcome by BMI, Age, and Pregnancy Risk



Grouped analysis of diabetes outcome by BMI category, age group, and pregnancy risk. Obesity and higher pregnancy counts correlate with greater diabetes prevalence.

title: Diabetes: EDA & Modeling
text:
Model Performance Comparison



Comparison of Logistic Regression vs Neural Network models. Logistic Regression provides balanced performance, while Neural Network struggles with recall and F1-score.

title: Diabetes: EDA & Modeling
text:
Logistic Regression Feature Importance



Feature importance from logistic regression coefficients. Diabetes Pedigree Function and BMI emerge as top predictors.

title: Diabetes: EDA & Modeling
text:
Neural Network Feature Importance



Neural network feature importance analysis. BMI, pregnancies, and glucose are the dominant drivers of prediction.

Delivered a reusable ETL script and database that cut data prep time in half.

text: Visuals

title: SolarSPELL: Survey ETL + MySQL + Analysis
section: Sentiment Analysis results of all free-text responses from a Survey
text:
Sentiment Analysis results of all free-text responses from a Survey



This was collected through ChatGPT’s API. All qualitative and free-text responses were collected and given a summary(theme) and sentiment score

title: SolarSPELL: Survey ETL + MySQL + Analysis
text:
Top Themes from Open-Ended Responses



Bar chart of the five most common themes explaining usefulness. “Resource availability” dominates, followed by affordability of technology, cost of books, cost of educational resources, and variety of tools.

title: SolarSPELL: Survey ETL + MySQL + Analysis
text:
Health-Related Searches in Lesotho



Horizontal bar chart of search terms matched on SolarSPELL devices. “Cholera” overwhelms other topics (≈934 queries), ahead of generic “disease” (~94), “heart” (~47), “ill” (~41), “diabetes” (~36), and “hand washing” (~34), indicating content demand and potential outreach priorities.

title: SolarSPELL: Survey ETL + MySQL + Analysis
section: CA Plots: Productivity Lift for Users
text:
CA Plots: Productivity Lift for Users



Slide showing boxplots for Conservation Agriculture (CA) plots. SolarSPELL users have higher and more consistent yields, with median productivity ~49.15 Kg/Are vs ~45.00 Kg/Are for non-users.

title: SolarSPELL: Survey ETL + MySQL + Analysis
section: SP Plots: Consistent Gains Across Methods
text:
SP Plots: Consistent Gains Across Methods



Standard Practice (SP) plots show the same pattern: users’ median productivity ~38.00 Kg/Are vs ~30.46 Kg/Are for non-users. The note highlights similar gains observed for other crops grown with CA, reinforcing broad utility.

title: SolarSPELL: Survey ETL + MySQL + Analysis
section: Knowledge Sharing: More Farmers Training Others
text:
Knowledge Sharing: More Farmers Training Others



Simple bar chart comparing the share of farmers who trained peers. SolarSPELL users are more likely to teach others—~82% vs ~77% among non-users—underscoring community diffusion effects.

title: SolarSPELL: Survey ETL + MySQL + Analysis
text:
The “Wow” Stat: Amplified Community Impact



Users train far more people on average (≈103 individuals per farmer) than non-users (≈42). The slide frames this as ROI and scalability: each user becomes a local knowledge hub.

title: SolarSPELL: Survey ETL + MySQL + Analysis
text:
Implications & Next Steps



Summary slide: (1) Proven model—evidence of better agricultural outcomes; (2) Leadership—users become educators, enabling sustainable development; (3) Expansion—strong case to target women coffee farmers to reduce gender gaps in access to information.
